chemicals.concentration_notes: ◦ Distribution: The toxin is found in the entire plant1. ◦ Potency: The severity of the symptoms is dose-dependent, meaning larger ingestions result in more severe irritation and clinical signs.
chemicals.description: ◦ Mucosal Irritation: The toxin acts as a potent irritant to mucous membranes upon contact or ingestion. ◦ Tissue Damage: This irritation can progress to ulcerations within the mouth and gastrointestinal tract. ◦ Systemic Effects: The irritation leads to abdominal discomfort, vomiting, and diarrhea, which can subsequently cause significant fluid loss and dehydration.
chemicals.name: The specific toxic compound has yet to be identified in veterinary literature, though it is classified as a gastrointestinal toxin

description:
Italian Arum (Arum spp., often Arum italicum) is an ornamental plant with arrow-shaped leaves and bright berries. It is unsafe for cats because the leaves, stems, tubers, and berries can all irritate the mouth and digestive tract.

The main problem is insoluble calcium oxalate crystals. These tiny, needle-like crystals are released when a cat bites the plant. They can scratch and burn the lips, tongue, mouth, and throat. The plant may also contain other irritating compounds, and the colorful berries can be especially tempting.

A cat that chews Italian arum may drool, paw at the mouth, vomit, or have trouble swallowing. Swelling in the mouth or throat can become serious. Keep the plant and loose berries away from cats, and call a veterinarian if your cat chews any part of it or shows mouth swelling, repeated vomiting, or breathing trouble.
name: Italian Arum
safetyNotes: Toxic compounds: insoluble calcium oxalate raphides, aroin (toxic protein), saponins; berries most concentrated
Mechanism: raphides cause immediate mechanical irritation to the oral and GI mucosa; aroin and saponins add systemic toxicity
Symptoms: intense oral burning, drooling, pawing at mouth, vomiting, diarrhea; severe berry ingestion may cause systemic illness
The attractive orange-red berries pose the greatest risk, particularly to inquisitive cats
Seek veterinary care if berry ingestion is suspected or if GI symptoms are severe

symptoms.name: Mucous Membrane Irritation and Ulcerations
symptoms.notes: The toxin causes direct irritation to the tissues it touches. In severe cases or large ingestions, this irritation progresses to the formation of actual ulcers within the mouth and digestive tract.
symptoms.onset: Acute (The irritation is a direct contact effect).

symptoms.name: Vomiting and Diarrhea
symptoms.notes: These are the primary systemic signs of ingestion.
symptoms.onset: Acute (Following the irritation of the gastric lining).

symptoms.name: Abdominal Pain / Discomfort
symptoms.notes: This pain results from the inflammation and irritation of the gastrointestinal tract lining caused by the plant's toxins.

symptoms.name: Dehydration
symptoms.notes: Dehydration is a significant concern following the fluid loss from vomiting and diarrhea. Rehydration and electrolyte replacement are key components of the recommended veterinary treatment.
symptoms.onset: Delayed (Occurs as a result of persistent vomiting and diarrhea).

treatments.description: The veterinarian administers pain relief medication to manage the discomfort caused by the toxin.
treatments.name: Administration of Analgesics
treatments.notes: This is necessary to treat the specific "oral mucosal irritation and pain" caused by the plant's toxins.

treatments.description: Fluids are administered (often intravenously) to restore hydration levels and balance electrolytes in the body.
treatments.name: Rehydration and Electrolyte Replacement
treatments.notes: This treatment is required to address dehydration resulting from the severe vomiting and diarrhea associated with Italian Arum ingestion.

treatments.description: Medication is given to suppress nausea and stop persistent vomiting.
treatments.name: Antiemetics
treatments.notes: This is used "as needed" to control the gastrointestinal distress and prevent further fluid loss.
